v2_vs_v4_scale_sensitivity: Nearly identical shape (100%→80%→~10% at scale 0/0.5/1.0 for both adapters); the cliff location does not meaningfully differ between v2 and v4, indicating the phenomenon is a general property of this LoRA training setup (target_modules/rank/data distribution shared across v2/v3/v4), not something newly introduced by v4's Phase4K data changes.

module_ablation_v4.note_on_bug: The 'full_v4' row inside phase4n_module_results.json was miscomputed (module_types=None was treated as 'apply to all layers' -> effectively scale=0.0 = base). The correct full_v4/scale=1.0 baseline below is taken from scale_sweep_v4.1.00_production_v4.

o_off.e36_note: no wrong name, cute tone retained

module_ablation_v4.conclusion: Disabling o_proj's LoRA contribution alone (q/k/v left at full strength) fully restores Q3 recall to base level (100%/100%) while avoiding the wrong-name hallucinations seen when q_proj or v_proj is disabled instead. o_proj is the single strongest module-level driver of the omission behavior found in this study.

layer_ablation_v4.conclusion: Almost any single-third ablation (whether removed or kept-alone) restores sampled recall to ~100%, indicating the omission behavior is a fragile, distributed effect that requires the full cumulative magnitude across all 48 layers acting together (all_on) to reliably reproduce -- it is not localized to one specific front/mid/back third. Name hallucination correlates loosely with mid/back involvement and is absent whenever a front-related condition is used.

promising_candidates_deepdive.generalization_conclusion: Both candidates' recall improvement generalizes beyond Q3 to Phase4I's independent held-out items (P01/P02), not a Q3-specific artifact.
promising_candidates_deepdive.Q11_NEW_finding: Both scale_0.25 and o_off REPLACE the known ループストック causal-fabrication with a NEW forbidden-category hallucination: unsolicited ヤメ時 (when-to-stop) advice, explicitly forbidden per Phase4K's data rules and previously flagged in Phase4L as a known-bad phrase pattern. Neither candidate is a clean fix on Q11 -- each trades one hallucination type for another.
promising_candidates_deepdive.important_caveat: This means 'reduce LoRA magnitude toward Base' does not cleanly separate persona-compression from unwanted behavior; it also partially un-suppresses Base's own tendency toward speculative advice-giving that training was specifically trying to control. The persona/recall/RAG-discipline trade-off is three-dimensional, not a simple two-axis persona-vs-recall dial.

capability_sacrificed_for_persona.q3_recall_full_v4_vs_base: 100% (scale=0.0/base) -> 10% avg sampled at production v4 (scale=1.0): a ~90 percentage-point sacrifice in RAG-enumeration recall attributable to the persona LoRA's cumulative magnitude.
capability_sacrificed_for_persona.held_out_recall_full_v4_vs_base: P01: 100%->50%, P02: 100%->40%, consistent with Q3's magnitude of degradation.
capability_sacrificed_for_persona.logits_shift_reference_from_phase4m: base-vs-adapter mean logit diff ~2.1-2.2 (large), inter-adapter (v2/v3/v4) diff ~0.09-0.15 (~15x smaller) -- consistent with this phase's finding that the omission behavior is governed primarily by shared LoRA-application magnitude/design rather than adapter-specific training differences.

final_judgment_explanation: Hypothesis D (data/objective-level cause, unfixable by application-time changes) is ruled out: Q3/P01/P02 all fully recover at low scale or with o_proj ablated. The clearest, most actionable, most strongly-supported single finding is module-level (Hypothesis C in the phase's lettering / labelled B here): o_proj's LoRA contribution is disproportionately responsible for the omission behavior, and disabling it alone (keeping q/k/v at full strength) is the most surgical intervention tested, fully restoring recall without introducing wrong-name persona hallucinations. This supports reconsidering target_modules (e.g., a lower LoRA rank/scale specifically on o_proj, or excluding it) for v5's design. However, the Q11 deep-dive shows that no scale/module choice tested is a clean win end-to-end: recovering RAG recall also re-admits Base's own tendency toward unsolicited advice-giving (a different forbidden-category hallucination). This is measured evidence that persona-compression and RAG-discipline are entangled with overall LoRA magnitude in ways not fully separable by inference-time scale/module tuning alone (a partial vote for Hypothesis E / architecture-reconsideration), so any v5 change should be validated end-to-end (recall AND hallucination AND persona) rather than optimizing recall alone.
